title: Long Non-Coding RNAs in Immune Thrombocytopenia: A Narrative Review of Pathogenesis and Clinical Implications
content: Background/Objectives: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune disease characterized by increased platelet destruction and insufficient platelet production. Accurate diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and treatment selection remain challenging. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate immune responses and may contribute to ITP pathogenesis. This review examines lncRNA expression in ITP and its potential diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance. Methods:  We reviewed English-language literature published between 1994 and 2026 using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. We examined studies of specific lncRNAs in ITP, focusing on their expression differences and potential diagnostic and therapeutic implications. Re-sults: The studies examined HCP5, NEAT1, lnc-DC, IFNG-AS1, MEG3, GAS5, MALAT1, and THRIL. Findings suggest these lncRNAs may contribute to ITP pathogenesis and serve as candidate diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. Some were reported as independent predictors of poor prognosis or were associated with glucocorticoid responsiveness. Potential applications include distinguishing primary from secondary ITP, informing patient selection for splenectomy, and identifying therapeutic targets. These applications remain investigational. Conclusions: Research on lncRNAs provides insight into autoimmune mechanisms underlying ITP and may support improvements in diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and individualized treatment. Although several lncRNAs show promise as biomarkers and therapeutic targets, further research, clinical validation, and methodological standardization are needed before routine clinical implementation.
